text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All newspapers report the parliament lifting the state of emergency, electing Rexhep Mejdani as the new president and nominating Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano as the new prime minister.

- Newspaper editorial says if Albania's new leaders start running the country with the same mistakes as the last Democratic party government their end will be quicker than that of President Sali Berisha.
- Fatos Nano, the new prime minister, will introduce his government at midday.
- The opposition Democratic Party said it considered the lifting of the state of emergency as hasty, unmotivated and unreasonable.
- Artan Santo was appointed as the new director of the state-owned Savings Bank of Albania.
- Army trucks went to the southern military base of Arshilengo in Gjirokaster district to collect remaining Chinese-made missiles after some 15 were stolen at the weekend.

- Newspaper editorial says the parliament has still not freed itself from political revenge as the opposition Democratic Party is not participating in its session, just like after the collapse of communism in 1991 and after rigged elections last year.
- The newly-elected President Rexhep Mejdani promised he would not be a party member any more but the president of all Albanians.
- Former President Berisha started working at an office in the opposition Democratic party.
- Oil smuggling in Montenegro and other illegal businesses supported the pyramid investment schemes in Albania, an IMF study says.
